title: How to Donate Your Body to Science
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss donating one's whole body to science. They cover the history of cadavers in anatomy education (executed criminals, grave robbing, "resurrectionists," and enslaved people's graves, including Chris Baker and Grandison Harris), religious views on body donation (Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, most other faiths), and the lack of centralized oversight compared with organ donation. They explain the practical process: family consent, body condition requirements (weight limits, disease exclusions), for-profit versus university donation and who pays for transport and cremation, and the timing of returned remains. They also cover uses such as car crash testing with cadavers, body exhibits like Body Worlds and Bodies, the University of Tennessee body farm, and a debate over profiting from body parts. The episode ends with listener mail about the submerged towns of Eureka, Montella, and Lackawack under the Rondout Reservoir.
topics: University of Tennessee Anthropology Research Facility

segments.title: Opening banter and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with small talk about Josh's congestion, then introduce the idea of donating one's body to science, noting that they had long promised an episode on it after the organ donation episode.

segments.title: Ethics, respect, and religious views
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the mental hurdle of having one's body dissected, the respectful treatment of donors by medical students, and religious objections. Islam is described as restrictive, Jehovah's Witnesses as opposed to blood transfusions but accepting bodies drained of blood, and most other faiths as generally accepting.
